name: Discrete mathematics
description: Sets, functions, counting, sequences and recurrences, with a first look at remainders and networks, taught at the Kepler outpost.
about:
Discrete mathematics realm ("Discrete mathematics"): sets, functions, exact counting, sequences and recurrences, and a first look at remainders and networks, for an
adult who has finished Foundations and nothing more. Same Kepler outpost, now with a Logistics Depot: crates, codes, crews and roads, and
Mira keeps the depot ledger. The concept plan is docs/plans/DISC-PLAN.md.

chapters.name: Sets and Venn diagrams
chapters.blurb: Sets, subsets, union, intersection, complement, Venn diagrams and pairs.

sector.name: Store Rooms
sector.purpose: know exactly what is in every bin

chapters.name: Functions and counting principles
chapters.blurb: Functions between finite sets, one-to-one and onto, and the two counting principles.

sector.name: Labelling Bay
sector.purpose: give every crate a label and every code a meaning

chapters.name: Arrangements and selections
chapters.blurb: Factorials, permutations, combinations, Pascal’s triangle and the binomial theorem.

sector.name: Crew Office
sector.purpose: count every way to pick and order a crew

chapters.name: Counting with conditions
chapters.blurb: Counting the complement, stars and bars, inclusion–exclusion and derangements.

sector.name: Packing Floor
sector.purpose: pack crates under every rule at once

chapters.name: Sequences
chapters.blurb: Closed and recursive formulas, arithmetic and geometric sequences, finite differences.

sector.name: Stock Yard
sector.purpose: forecast stock that grows by a rule

chapters.name: Recurrences and generating functions
chapters.blurb: Solving recurrences, counting tilings, generating functions and counting two ways.

sector.name: Tiling Works
sector.purpose: count patterns that are built one step at a time

chapters.name: First steps into numbers and networks
chapters.blurb: Remainders and clock arithmetic, graphs, trees and Euler paths.

sector.name: Road Office
sector.purpose: number the codes and map the roads between the domes

source.label: Levin and OpenStax

source.example: Levin, Discrete Mathematics: An Open Introduction — 1.3 Combinations and Permutations

mentor.name: Mira
mentor.opening: I’m Mira. The depot is full, and we have to {purpose}. Your task is “{title}.” {brief} The idea we need: {topic}.
mentor.closing: You already have everything this needs from Foundations. I’ll work the first example with you, and the guided steps are there whenever you want them.

copy.homeTitle:
Everything here can be counted.
Learn to count it cleverly.
copy.firstVisit: Welcome back. The depot is overflowing with crates, codes, crews and roads, and nobody knows how many ways there are to arrange them. We begin by listing what is in one bin; everything you need you learned in Foundations.
copy.allDone: You did it. The depot ledger is complete, and every count in it is exact. Number theory and Graph theory each pick up a thread from the Road Office.
copy.chaptersNote: Seven chapters. Learn every concept in a chapter to unlock a landmark for the depot. Practice missions are optional.

skills.title: The skill tree
skills.text: Follow the prerequisite branches from sets to graphs. Each mission you finish opens the ideas that are built on it.

visual.title: The concept bench
visual.text: Pick any mission, change its numbers and predict the count before you check it. Nothing here affects your progress, and it all works offline.

help.title: Count it without listing it.
help.intro: Discrete maths starts where Foundations ends: with sets, functions and simple counting. It teaches how to count arrangements, selections, sequences and networks exactly, without writing every case out. Every new word and symbol is explained before you are asked to use it, with a worked example first.
help.answers: Answers are whole numbers, such as a count, a term or a degree, never a set or a list. Type them without commas or spaces (1250, not 1,250). A yes or no is typed as 1 or 0, and a choice is typed as the code shown in the prompt.

concepts.q04: Complement, difference and |A ∪ B| = |A| + |B| − |A ∩ B| [CM 1.4, Levin 0.3]
concepts.q07: Functions between finite sets: domain, codomain, image [Levin 0.4]
concepts.q15: Pascal's triangle, bit strings and the 2ⁿ subsets [Levin 1.2]
concepts.q17: Chapter review: order or no order? [Levin 1.3]
concepts.q28: Recurrence relations and the Fibonacci numbers [Levin 2.1, 2.4]
concepts.q32: Counting with recurrences: tilings and spaced-out bit strings [Levin 2.4]
concepts.q33: Generating functions: reading off a coefficient [Levin 5.1]
concepts.q37: Graphs, degrees and the handshake lemma [Levin 4.1]
concepts.q40: Realm review and bridge to Number theory and Graph theory [Levin 5.2, 4.5]
